title: Far-impostor instance caps overflow in eras 1-2 and truncate in grid-scan order, deforesting the northern third of the map
area: src/vegetation.js — far tier fill (setEra) + placementsFor grid
evidence: placementsFor builds far lists by scanning the 9m grid south-to-north (vegetation.js:369-372), and setEra keeps only the first `n = Math.min(arr.length, farM.instanceMatrix.count)` entries (vegetation.js:528) — no centre-out sort like grass.js uses. Runtime probe on the built artifact (artifact/brezgi-taurene.html via window.__scene): era 1 far meshes ALL saturated at cap — spruce 175000/175000, pine 125000/125000, birch 150000/150000, oak 42000/42000 — with the last-filled instance at z=4345/3775/4072/1846 respectively while the map spans to z=6040 (Brežģa kalns z=4969, Krogs z=5270). Era 2 same, cutoffs 4982/4399/4894/2215. Screenshots (scratchpad/audit/brezga-north-era1.png, brezga-north-era2.png, era 1 nofog from (1728,1100,3700) toward Brežģa kalns): the 'near-closed-canopy primeval forest' era shows bare meadow with exactly two isolated 260m tree discs — the FULL_R full-detail circles around the BREZGA and KROGS POIs whose lists don't overflow — because every far impostor north of the cutoff was silently dropped. Paradoxically eras 3/4 (agrarian) have MORE forest around Brežģa kalns than AD 50.
fix_hint: Make far-tier truncation spatially unbiased: if arr.length > cap, stride-subsample (keep every arr.length/cap-th entry) or sort by distance to the POI set before truncating; alternatively scale the keep-probability in placementsFor by cap/expected per species, or raise CAPS for eras 1-2 densities.
why: Every element of the finding checks out against the current code and a fresh runtime probe. (1) Code: src/vegetation.js placementsFor fills far lists by scanning the 9m grid with iz ascending = z ascending, i.e. south-to-north (lines 369-372, z range [-2640,6040] from HM_SPAN=8800/HM_OFF_Z=1700), and setEra truncates to the first n=Math.min(arr.length, farM.instanceMatrix.count) entries (line 528) with no stride-subsample or spatial sort — unlike grass.js:287-299 which deliberately sorts centre-out so overflow drops the rim, never one side. (2) Runtime: my independent puppeteer probe on artifact/brezgi-taurene.html reproduced the reviewer's numbers exactly — era 1 far meshes saturated at cap (spruce 175000, pine 125000, birch 150000, oak 42000) with max placed z of 4352/3775/4072/1846 respectively; era 2 cutoffs 4982/4406/4902/2215; Brežģa kalns is at z=4969 and Krogs at z=5270, so both lie beyond most cutoffs. Eras 3/4 do not saturate and their far placements reach z=6040, confirming the paradox that agrarian eras show more northern forest than the primeval eras. (3) Visual: my own fresh screenshots (verify-north-era1.png vs verify-north-era3.png, cam 1728,1100,3500 toward the hill, fog disabled) show era 1's north as bare meadow with exactly two isolated FULL_R=260m full-detail tree discs around the BREZGA and KROGS POIs, while era 3 from the identical viewpoint is visibly more forested. Severity high is fair: the flagship primeval era silently deforests roughly the northern third of the map including the two family-heritage POIs the sim is named for.

title: Grass hiOff aerial band-shedding can never trigger: main.js passes camera.position as both focus and camPos, so camDist is always 0
evidence: main.js:516 `const focus = camera.position;` then main.js:529 `grass.update(focus, currentEra, camera.position)` — the same Vector3 object twice. grass.js:416 computes camDist = |camPos − focus| = 0 every frame, so nearOn is always true and the documented aerial path (grass.js:414-425: drop turf/carpet/near, extend mid to r0Dyn=0, mesh0Off) is dead code. Verified on the built artifact: with the camera at 800m altitude (era 4, cam (117,990,740)), band meshes report turf 20735/20735, carpet 45969/49532, near 30626/30626, mid 47429 — all fully populated and regenerating around the ground point under the camera, exactly the '~100k subpixel instances / rings read as discs' case the code comments say this logic exists to prevent.
fix_hint: Pass a real ground focus (rig target / controls.target) as focus, or compute camDist inside grass.update as camPos.y − heightAt(focus.x, focus.z) so height above terrain drives nearOn.
why: Verified both statically and at runtime. main.js:516/529 pass camera.position as both focus and camPos (same Vector3, only call site), so grass.js:416 camDist is always 0 and nearOn is always true; since bands init with on:true (grass.js:232), the toggle at grass.js:418 never fires and the aerial shed path (hiOff off, mid.r0Dyn=0, mesh0Off) is unreachable dead code. Independent puppeteer probe on the built artifact with the camera at y=990 (era 4) reproduced the reviewer's exact counts — turf 20735/20735, near 30626/30626, carpet 45969/49532, mid 47429/53015 — all hiOff bands fully populated at aerial altitude, and the screenshot shows the dense grass disc rendered under the camera that this logic was written to prevent. Severity med and fix hint (use rig/simControls target or height-above-terrain) are appropriate.

title: Orchards ignore the eras.js skip() zone, planting houseless apple orchards inside stead/manor/krogs grounds — breaking the documented farmSiteKept contract
area: src/vegetation.js:444-452 orchard loop vs src/eras.js:248 bgSettlement
evidence: landuse.js:376-378 documents farmSiteKept as shared by buildings and orchards 'so one farm never gets an orchard without a house'. But eras.js:237-248 additionally suppresses houses via skip() (within 100m of STEAD, 140m of MANOR, 70m of KROGS/BREZGA, 80m of POND, 60m of CAMP) while vegetation.js:445 only checks farmSiteKept — every kept skip-zone site gets 2-4 apple trees with no dwelling. Concrete DWELLINGS_OSM sites (geodata-osm.js): 'Kaltu māja' (−170,60) is 24m from STEAD (−183,40); Rudiņi (−53,−98), Dadzis (−36,−147), Nēķins 1/2 (−123,−76 / −127,−122), Cimbulīši (48,−203), Neķina muiža (−135,−228), Senkrasti (−106,−296) are all within 140m of MANOR (−40,−180); 'Brežģis' (2353,5276) is 33m from KROGS (2320,5270). In era 4 farmSiteKept keeps 96% of sites, so nearly all of these orphan orchards exist. bgFieldsFor (landuse.js:229-234) has the same divergence for background fields.
fix_hint: Export the POI-proximity skip predicate from landuse.js (next to farmSiteKept) and apply it in vegetation.js's orchard loop and landuse.js's bgFieldsFor, so buildings, orchards and fields share one site-existence rule.
why: Every claim checks out against the current code. landuse.js:375-380 documents farmSiteKept as the single site-existence rule shared by buildings, orchards and yard props "so one farm never gets an orchard without a house". But eras.js:237-239/254 additionally suppresses background dwellings via skip() (STEAD 100m, MANOR 140m, KROGS/BREZGA 70m, POND 80m, CAMP 60m), while vegetation.js:444-445 plants 2-4 apple trees per kept site checking only farmSiteKept, and bgFieldsFor (landuse.js:233-234) has the identical divergence for fields. Recomputing with the real data (rvx=-393 so STEAD=(-183,40)): era 4 has exactly 9 kept skip-zone sites getting houseless orchards — Kaltu maja 24m from STEAD; Dadzis 33m, Rudini 83m, Cimbulisi 91m, Nekins 2 105m, Nekina muiza 106m, Nekins 1 133m, Senkrasti 133m from MANOR (also 50m from POND); Brezgis 34m from KROGS — and era 3 has 7 (plus Brezgu Pienotava, buildingless in era 3 via the pienotava rule yet still orcharded). The trees are not culled elsewhere: dPOI at vegetation.js:450 only picks the LOD tier, and the full-tier apple count (66 orchard + 12 stead = 78) is under the 110 instance cap with orphans placed first, so none are dropped. Screenshots of era 4 (manor-north-era4.png, nekins1-close-era4.png) show the isolated apple trees standing in open grass at the computed Nekins/Rudini positions with no dwelling. Minor caveats only: the skip() cite is line 254 (definition 237-239), and the visual impact is subtle (trees read as ordinary landscape trees), so severity med is the ceiling — but the code-contract breach and its concrete consequences are exactly as described.

title: regenFlowers consumes the rim-feather rng draw conditionally on camera distance, so flowers in boundary cells teleport/change species between regens (eras 1-2)
evidence: Per flower the loop draws x,z,rot,sc,pick (5 draws) then hits `if (d > R || d < 3) continue;` (grass.js:260) BEFORE the rim draw `if (rng() < smoothstepJ(R*0.75,R,d)) continue;` (grass.js:261) — d depends on the camera focus, so whether the 6th draw is consumed is camera-dependent, shifting every later flower's draw tuple in that cell. This contradicts the file's stable-world contract (lines 5-8) and the blade loop's own fixed-order rule (grass.js:339-343, which deliberately draws all 9 values before any conditional continue). Only eras 1-2 are affected (perCell=1.12 gives n=2 cells; eras 3+ have n≤1). Exact replication of the cell loop with util.js mulberry32/cellSeed (era 1, salt 52): cell(−40,5) renders its second flower at (−238.82, 35.71, rot .572, sc .305) when the walker stands on flower0, but at (−234.29, 33.43, rot .305, sc .989) from a focus 30m away — a ~5m teleport with all draws shifted one slot. An in-page A/B test at one meadow spot showed 0 mismatches, confirming the event is rare (needs an n=2 cell straddling the d<3 hole or R=125 rim), hence low severity.
fix_hint: Draw the rim-gate value unconditionally with the other per-flower draws (const rim = rng() alongside pick), then apply the d-range and rim tests.
why: Verified against src/grass.js: the rim-feather draw (line 261) is consumed only when the camera-dependent d-range test (line 260) passes, after 5 unconditional per-flower draws (lines 257-258) — so in n=2 cells the second flower's x/z/rot/sc/pick shift one rng slot depending on camera focus. Exact replication with the production mulberry32/cellSeed reproduced the reviewer's numbers: cell(−40,5), era 1, salt 52 has n=2, and flower1 renders at (−238.82, 35.71) when the walker stands 1.4 m from flower0 (d<3 hole, rim draw skipped) but at (−234.29, 33.43) from a focus 30 m away (rim draw consumed) — a ~5 m teleport with pick flipping 0.989→0.070, changing species via line 267. This contradicts the file's stable-world contract (lines 5-8) and the blade loop's deliberate fixed-order draw rule (lines 339-343). Era scoping confirmed: perCell=1.12 in eras 1-2 yields n=2 in ~11.9% of cells; eras 3+ have n≤1 so no later flower can shift. Low severity is appropriate — the event needs an n=2 cell whose first flower crosses the d<3 hole or R=125 rim between regen foci. Fix hint (draw the rim gate unconditionally with the other per-flower draws) is correct; later continues consume no rng.

title: Turf and near grass bands saturate exactly at cap in open meadow — the 0.75 headroom factor underestimates survival, silently chopping the outer feather cells
evidence: grass.js:225 sizes caps as full-disc cells × perCell × 0.75 with the comment 'rules thin ~40%+; headroom', but in open terrain the only culls are the rim feathers (~13%), so demand ≈ 0.87 × full > cap. Probe on the built artifact at an ordinary era-4 meadow regen: turf 20735/20735 and near 30626/30626 — count equals capacity exactly, meaning the centre-out loop (grass.js:301 `if (i >= cap) break`) is discarding the outermost cells every regen; carpet is at 93% (45969/49532) and mid at 89% (47429/53015). Effect is mostly masked because each band's truncated rim happens to fall under the next band's ramp-in overlap, but the designed feathered cross-fades (grass.js:346-348) are cut to hard cell-boundary edges at ~24m (turf) and ~51m (near), and the stated headroom assumption is wrong.
fix_hint: Compute caps from the actual annulus area with a worst-case (open-meadow) survival fraction ~0.9, or clamp perCell so worst-case demand fits cap; optionally log/assert when i hits cap during regenerate.
why: Code check: grass.js:224-225 sizes each band cap as full-disc cells × perCell × 0.75 ("rules thin ~40%+; headroom"), and grass.js:299-302 fills cells centre-out with `if (i >= cap) break`, silently dropping outermost cells on overflow. Analytically, for the r0=0 bands (turf, near) the only open-terrain cull is the outer feather (grass.js:347-348), giving ~87% survival, so open-meadow demand/cap ≈ 1.13 — the 0.75 headroom assumption is wrong. Empirically (own headless probe on the built artifact, era 4, FPS-governor pinned at level 0 so grass budget=1): at 3 of 4 open-meadow spots turf hit exactly 20735/20735 and near exactly 30626/30626 (saturated at cap, matching the finding's numbers), and radial histograms prove hard truncation — saturated turf has zero instances beyond ~23.4m (design r1=26; an unsaturated spot feathers smoothly to 25.99m) and saturated near zero beyond ~48.8m (design r1=55). Carpet (~98%) and mid (~89-99%) stay under cap, and the cut edges fall inside the next band's ramp-in, confirming the masking and low severity. Minor discrepancies only: measured edges ~23.4m/~48.8m vs claimed ~24m/~51m, and the break statement is line 302 not 301.

title: bgFieldsFor places crop fields in the Gauja, in lakes and across roads — no placement checks at all
area: src/landuse.js:230-247 (bgFieldsFor), consumed by fieldsIndexed/fieldAt and terrain paint
evidence: bgFieldsFor only checks farmSiteKept(si,era); field centres go 60-120m from the dwelling in a random direction with rx up to 84m, with no test against river, lakes, streams, roads, or the stage-skip zones. Verified by loading geodata.js/geodata-osm.js + landuse.js in node and intersecting sampled ellipse interiors with the rendered water (river half-width 11.8m from water.js ribbon; lake polys; ROADS_OSM+hand roads via distToRoadEx): era 3 = 14/211 bg fields intersect the open river channel (worst 38% of area at cx,cz=(-1431,3147)); era 4 = 23/334 on the river (three ~30%-submerged fields right at the mill-pond stage bend: (-179,-265) potato, (22,-450) potato, (86,-460) flax), 2 inside Brenkūzis lake (rye field at (-652,2834) is 89% under the lake), 3 on streams; 62 (era 3) / 117 (era 4) fields overlap a road carriageway (up to 26% of area). paintEra applies field colour+plough striping before the water-margin overrides, so crop paint runs down both banks to the waterline (visible in scratchpad/audit/y1-e4-pond-close.png lower-left: fallow/dirt field paint reaching the channel edge at the pond bend, which is exactly where view=muiza looks). Full numbers: scratchpad/audit/xmod-out2.txt.
fix_hint: In bgFieldsFor, resample the (angle,dist) draw while the candidate ellipse fails cheap tests: distToRiver(cx,cz) < rx+16, distToStreams < rx+5, lake bbox+pointInPoly, distToRoadEx(era).d < 0, and the same skip() zones eras.js uses; 2-3 retries from the same per-site rng keeps it deterministic.
why: Core claim verified against current code and my own measurements. (1) Code: bgFieldsFor (src/landuse.js:230-247) checks only farmSiteKept — field centres go 60-120m from each OSM dwelling in a random direction with rx up to ~84m and no test against river, streams, lakes, roads, or the skip() stage zones that eras.js:237-254 applies to the same sites' buildings. (2) Independent numeric probe (esbuild-bundled real modules, 13x13 ellipse sampling, conservative 10.2m channel half-width vs the 11.8m ribbon): era 3 = 13/211 bg fields intersect the open river channel and 59 overlap a road carriageway (distToRoadEx.d<0, worst 25% of area); era 4 = 21/334 on the river, 2 inside Brenkūzis lake (rye at (-652,2834) is 90% inside the lake polygon, matching the claimed 89%), 118 road overlaps (worst 30%). The three claimed era-4 pond-bend fields exist; two have centres 4.9m and 7.8m from the river centreline, i.e. inside the open channel. (3) My own screenshots confirm visibility: v-e4-nw-fallow.png shows a brown fallow field straddling the Gauja with crop paint to the waterline on both banks; v-e3-bend-fallow.png shows fallow fields merging with the pond-bend road junction across the river. Minor caveats that do not overturn the finding: the '3 fields on streams' sub-claim did not reproduce (0 hits at the 3.7m stream ribbon half-width); road overlaps are visually tempered because paintEra paints roads after fields (terrain.js:365 vs 376) so the carriageway stays visible; the 90%-submerged lake field is mostly hidden by the lake mesh and wet-margin paint, so lake severity is lower than the river case. Exact per-field worst-case percentages differ slightly from the reporter's (likely different sampling/threshold), but the pattern, the specific field coordinates, and the visible river artifact all hold.

title: Cross-module ghost farms: orchards and fields spawn at sites that bgSettlement skips near the stage anchors
evidence: bgSettlement drops DWELLINGS_OSM sites within 100m of STEAD / 140m of MANOR / 70m KROGS / 70m BREZGA / 80m POND / 60m CAMP, but vegetation.js orchards and landuse.js bgFieldsFor gate only on farmSiteKept — so those sites get apple trees and 1-2 crop fields with no buildings. On real data: 6 sites in era 3, 9 in era 4 (sites 99, 101, 103-104, 125-128, 4). Site 99 at (-170,60) is 23m from the STEAD anchor and its first orchard tree lands at (-169,47) — inside the hand-built riku fence of the Brezgi farmyard (fence spans x -210..-156, z 18..66); sites 125-127 put orchards/fields in the manor grounds, site 4 at the krogs (33m). Verified by exact replication in scratchpad/audit/xmod-audit.mjs (output xmod-out2.txt).
fix_hint: Move the skip() predicate into landuse.js next to farmSiteKept (e.g. export siteActive(si,era) = farmSiteKept && !nearAnchor) and use it in all three call sites, so house+orchard+fields stay an atomic unit.
why: Verified independently against the live code, not the reviewer's script. (1) eras.js:237-239/254 applies skip() (STEAD 100m/MANOR 140m/KROGS 70m/BREZGA 70m/POND 80m/CAMP 60m) to background buildings AND yard props, while vegetation.js:444-453 (orchards) and landuse.js:230-247 (bgFieldsFor) gate only on farmSiteKept — breaking the invariant documented at landuse.js:375-377 ("one farm never gets an orchard without a house"). (2) Exact replication importing the real modules reproduces the claim: 6 ghost sites in era 3 (99,101,104,125,126,127), 9 in era 4 (4,99,101,103,104,125,126,127,128). Site 99 "Kaltu māja" (-170,60) is 24m from STEAD; its first orchard tree lands at exactly (-169,47), inside the hand-built riku fence loop (eras.js:541-543, corners S.x-27..S.x+28, S.z-22..S.z+26 = x -210..-155, z 18..66) — and 2m from the hand-placed cart at (-169,49). Site 4 is 34m from the krogs; sites 103/104/125-128 ring the manor at 33-133m, each with 1-2 crop fields (centers 40-229m from the manor/stead). Claimed distances (23m/33m) differ by 1m rounding only. (3) Nothing culls the ghosts downstream: fillTier instances every entry (apple full tier 78/110 in era 4, incl. 29 ghost trees), terrain field paint runs regardless of anchors. (4) Screenshot evidence (scratchpad/audit/v-stead-e4-crop.png): era-4 stead yard shows the ghost apple tree standing inside the fence directly over the cart; v-manor-e4-crop.png shows clusters of 2-4 lone trees ringing empty meadow near the manor where the skipped dwellings would stand. Severity med and the proposed fix (share one siteActive predicate across all three call sites) are appropriate.

title: Background dwellings/barns/klēts are placed inside road carriageways, including a house on the P30 highway
evidence: The dwelling rectangle is placed at the raw OSM site and the barn/klēts at random 12-23m offsets with no distToRoadEx test. On current HEAD data: era 3 has 9 items and era 4 has 11 items whose centre is >1m inside a carriageway; worst cases: dwelling at (0,-353) sits on the class-0 P30 in both eras (d=-3.1m, i.e. ~2m from the asphalt ribbon centreline), klets (-146,122) 4.6m into a lane, barn (-263,-317) 2.3m into a V-road; era 5 has 7 OSM footprints >1m inside painted lanes (e.g. (-147,137) at 6.5m). Road ribbons/paint draw straight through these buildings. Data: scratchpad/audit/xmod-out2.txt section 3.
fix_hint: After computing each item position, reject/re-roll if distToRoadEx(era,x,z).d < max(w,d)/2 + 1 (re-draw the yard angle from the same per-site rng); for the era-5 OSM footprints, only skip when the overlap is with a class 0/1 ribbon road.
why: CONFIRMED by code reading, exact numeric reproduction with the real modules, and fresh screenshots. (1) src/eras.js:247-271 places the dwelling box at the raw DWELLINGS_OSM point and the barn/klets at random 15-23m / 12-18m offsets; the only filters are skip() (proximity to the 6 diorama anchors, eras.js:237-239) and farmSiteKept — no distToRoadEx test anywhere in bgSettlement; era 5 places raw BUILDINGS_OSM footprints with skip() only. (2) A probe importing the real distToRoadEx/farmSiteKept/mulberry32 (aliases per eras.js:24) reproduces the finding's data exactly: era 3 = 9 items, era 4 = 11, era 5 = 7 with centre >1m inside the road metric, including dwelling 'Dispečeri' (0,-353) at d=-3.1 on the class-0 P30 in both eras (raw distance 1.5m from the centreline vs the 3.2m drawn ribbon half-width, eras.js:144), klets (-147,122) d=-4.6, barn (-263,-317) d=-2.3 (raw 0.4m from a V-road centreline, inside its 2.4m ribbon), and era-5 OSM footprint (-147,137) d=-6.5. roadRibbons renders class 0/1 ribbons in eras 3/4/5 (eras.js:588,628) and terrain paint draws all roads at full strength where d<-1 (terrain.js:377-388), so every listed item sits in a visible carriageway. (3) Screenshots: p30-house-era4.png shows the P30 gravel ribbon running into and re-emerging beyond the grey-roofed dwelling at (0,-353); pandera-era4.png shows the tan dwelling seated on the painted village-road band at (-145,137); pandera-era5.png shows the 40m OSM shed occupying the lane corridor. Two immaterial nits: the flagship raw offset is ~1.5m (not ~2m) from the ribbon centreline, and the 'class 2 lane' hits at the (-145,137) cluster are actually the hand-laid diorama roads (c defaults to 2 in roadGridFor, landuse.js:348, w=5.5) rather than OSM lanes — still painted carriageways, so the defect and the proposed fix (reject/re-roll when distToRoadEx(era,x,z).d < max(w,d)/2 + 1) stand.

title: bgSettlement buildings sit on a single centre heightAt sample — corners float up to 2.6m or bury 2.5m on slopes
evidence: Sampling heightAt at the four rotated footprint corners of every placed item: era 5 has 18/476 buildings with a corner gap >0.7m (worst 2.64m under the 40x11m shed at (77,-425)) and 16 buried >1.2m at a corner (worst 2.52m at (1190,2333)); era 4 worst float 0.86m at (6,-381). Screenshot scratchpad/audit/y2-e5-float-close.png shows the shed at (445,-448) (computed float 2.24m) overhanging the river bank with open water visible under its corner. The 0.15m sink only covers gentle ground; riverside and moraine slopes exceed it by an order of magnitude.
fix_hint: Sample heightAt at the 4 corners in bgSettlement, set y = min(corner) - 0.15 and stretch wallH by (max-min) so the ridge stays put while walls extend into the slope; or skip sites where max-min > ~2.5m.
why: Verified all three legs of the finding against the current code. (1) Code: src/eras.js:295 sets `const y = heightAt(it.x, it.z) - 0.15` — one centre sample per building; bgAssets (src/eras.js:214-215) is a unit box translated +0.5 so the wall base sits exactly at y, leaving only the fixed 0.15m sink to absorb slope. (2) Numeric reproduction: I imported the real heightAt from src/terrain.js in Node, replicated bgSettlement's item generation exactly (BUILDINGS_OSM + skip() for era 5; DWELLINGS_OSM + farmSiteKept + mulberry32 seeds for era 4), and sampled the 4 rotated footprint corners: era 5 has 476 items with 18 corner floats >0.7m (worst 2.64m under the 40x11.1 shed at (77,-425)) and 17 buried >1.2m (worst 2.52m at (1190,2333), 27.3x25); the shed at (445,-448) floats 2.24m at its corner (434.8,-439.6) — base 186.46 over ground 184.22 — while its opposite corner buries 1.88m; era 4 worst float 0.86m at (6,-381). These match the finding's figures almost exactly (only 17 vs claimed 16 buried, a trivial threshold/convention difference). (3) Visual: my own era-5 screenshots (scratchpad/audit/w-corner-445.png, w-corner-445b.png, w-corner-77.png) show the (445,-448) shed's base edge airborne over the dropping river bank — the from-below shot at camera y=185.2 sees the box's underside with open space beneath — and the (77,-425) shed's near corner floating above the falling ground. The proposed fix direction (min-corner base + wall stretch, or skipping extreme sites) is sound.

title: BRIDGE2 deck does not span the rendered channel — it ends in open water in every era that places it
area: src/eras.js:555-557 and 618-619 (bridge at BRIDGE2, rot hardcoded PI/2); src/landuse.js:187 (BRIDGE2 anchored to raw river point)
evidence: BRIDGE2 = riverPointNearest(0,-400) = raw point (-37,-423), but the water ribbon follows the Catmull-Rom spline which bulges off the raw polyline on exactly this bend, and the local flow direction ((91,-55) normalized) is ~31 degrees off the x-axis, so the fixed z-oriented 28m deck needs 27.6m of reach perfectly centred — any spline offset leaves an end in the water. Screenshots: scratchpad/audit/y1-e4-pond-close.png (deck starts on the west bank and terminates mid-river) and y3-e4-pole-field-river.png right edge (same bridge from the north, left end in the water).
fix_hint: Anchor the bridge to sampleSpline at the nearest t (the true rendered centreline), set rot = atan2 of the local spline tangent + PI/2, and size the deck to distance-between-banks (walk meshHeightAt until above water level on each side) + 3m.
why: Verified numerically and visually. BRIDGE2 is anchored at raw RIVER_PTS point (-37,-423) (landuse.js:190-192) and the bridge is placed with hardcoded rot=PI/2 in eras 3/4 (eras.js:555) and era 5 (eras.js:618). Local flow direction (91,-55) is 31° off the x-axis, so the 28m z-oriented deck crosses the channel obliquely: deck-end centres land ~11.9-12.1m perpendicular from the rendered centreline while the water ribbon edge is at 11.8m and one corner of each end is at ~10.9-11.2m — over open flat water. Worse, the terrain carve (terrain.js:58) keeps ground below water level out to 16m from the spline, so dry bank starts only ~19m from the bridge centre along the deck axis — 5m beyond each deck end. Fresh screenshots (vb2-e4-north-low.png, vb2-e4-close-top.png, vb2-e5-close-top.png) show the deck ends hovering over open water in eras 4 and 5; era 3 shares the identical code path. One correction to the finding's stated mechanism: the Catmull-Rom spline interpolates its control points, so the bridge centre lies exactly on the rendered centreline — the defect comes from the fixed PI/2 rotation and the submerged shelf width, not from a spline bulge at the anchor. The defect itself and the fix hint (rotate deck to spline tangent + PI/2, size to bank-to-bank) hold.

title: farmSiteKept era-3 sites are not a subset of era-4: six farms exist in 1860 and vanish by 1935, inverting the stated model

Code: src/eras.js:137 sets era-5 asphalt to 0x393c40; line 144 gives the P30 (c:0) a 6.4 m width (half=3.2); lines 169-171 contain the CCW winding fix; lines 148+173+178-179 paint the centreline on every other ~9 m resample span at 0.18 m width (half-width 0.09), i.e. ~9 m dash / ~9 m gap — exactly the oversized cadence the finding reports vs the ~3 m/9 m, 0.10-0.15 m real-world standard. title: River reads as an elevated canal behind a dyke: floodplain carved below waterline while the bank skirt stays pinned at water level
evidence: src/terrain.js:43 stamps the valley to target p[2]-1.8 (1.8 m BELOW water) with inner radius 17 m / outer 50 m, and :55-58 add spline stamps to y-1.9 (r=26/9) and y-0.55 (r=30/16). Measured cross-sections (node import of src/terrain.js heightAt): at z=40 terrain is 183.4-184.5 from 12-35 m off the centreline vs water 185.0; at z=1200 terrain <185 out to 24-45 m; even at the steep manor bend the 14.5-20 m shelf is 183.3-184.9. Meanwhile src/water.js:229-232 builds the skirt rows at fixed y-0.5 / y+0.04 / y+0.07 — it never calls heightAt, contradicting its own comment (water.js:155-157 'outer verts drape onto the terrain'). Walking-level screenshots audit/e1-A-east.png, e1-A-west.png, e4-A-east.png, e1-C-east.png and crop-A-edge.png show the water surface visibly higher than the surrounding meadow, held by a vertical tan wall (the skirt seen edge-on), with a sunken pale floodplain behind it — in both era 1 and era 4.
fix_hint: Keep the deep trench only under the ribbon (dist < ~13 m of the fine spline) and clamp the carve to >= local water level +0.2 beyond the skirt width; and/or make the skirt真 drape: sample heightAt for the outer verts and extend the collar until it meets ground that is above water.
why: Every claim reproduced against current code. terrain.js:43 stamps ground to waterline-1.8m with inner radius 17m (fully below water at 17m, blending back only by 50m), and terrain.js:55/58 add y-1.9 (r26/9) and y-0.55 (r30/16) spline stamps — verbatim as cited. water.js:229-232 builds the bank skirt at fixed y-0.5/y+0.04/y+0.07 relative to water level; heightAt is imported (water.js:8) but never called in the file, contradicting the 'outer verts drape onto the terrain' comment at water.js:155-157; skirt outer width is only 12.9-17.3m (water.js:175). Independent measurement (esbuild-bundled heightAt, 2000 perpendicular cross-sections): at 18m offset — beyond the skirt's maximum reach — terrain is below the local waterline in 91.2% of samples (mean 1.15m, max 2.24m below), still 48.6% at 30m; the cited cross-sections at z≈40 (ground 183.3-184.3 vs water 185.0) and the manor bend reproduce. My own fresh walking-level screenshots (v-e4-across.png era 4 at village centre, v-e1-oblique.png era 1) both show the water plane visibly above the adjacent meadow, held by a tan edge-on skirt wall with a sunken floodplain behind — the elevated-canal artefact exactly as described, in both eras. The finding if anything understates the extent: ~91% of the river length is affected just beyond the skirt.

title: Gauja meander at the Dzerbe confluence: water ribbons float in mid-air over a pan carved 1.9 m below river level
evidence: RIVER_PTS legs of the meander loop are 40-60 m apart, so the overlapping y-1.9 spline stamps (src/terrain.js:52-58) excavate the whole loop interior: measured heightAt = 176.5-176.8 across (1495,-460)-(1600,-450) vs local river level 178.0-178.4 and Dzerbe stream end 178.8 (points are NOT inside the Taurenes ezers polygon, level 178.7, verified by point-in-poly test). why: Reproduced numerically against the actual code and visually with fresh screenshots. Importing src/terrain.js heightAt in Node: along the reviewer's strip (1495,-460)->(1600,-450) terrain = 176.15-176.79 vs local river water level 178.0-178.4 (1.2-1.9 m below water), with every point outside the Taurenes ezers polygon (verified with the project's own pointInPoly). A 5 m-grid scan of the loop (x 1440-1640, z -570..-410) shows 425/849 cells lying beyond the 14.5 m max reach of water ribbon (half-width 11.8 m, src/water.js:149) + bank skirt (W_OUT 14.5, src/water.js:160) and outside the lake are below water level (worst 1.93 m below at 1515,-465). Fresh screenshots (v-loop-aerial/v-loop-south/v-loop-onpan, plus era-4 v-loop-south-e4 in scratchpad/audit) show the barren tan pan filling the loop interior with the water surface and its rim edges hanging above it, identical in eras 1 and 4 — matching the reported floating-slab appearance. One mechanism correction: the stamps do NOT compound (terrain.js:23 field0 copy + line 38-39 min-candidate keeps overlapping stamps idempotent); the carve comes from single wide stamps — the r=50/inner=17 point stamps targeting y-1.8 (terrain.js:43) and r=26/inner=9 spline stamps targeting y-1.9 (terrain.js:55) — whose full-depth zones from one meander leg reach across the 25-50 m-wide loop interior (RIVER_PTS [1463,-471]..[1533,-440], Dzerbe end [1493,-544]), well beyond the 11.8 m water coverage. The observable defect, location, magnitude, and era claims all hold; only the 'stamps compound' phrasing and the second fix-hint option are slightly off, the first fix-hint (clamp terrain >= water level + margin beyond ~13 m from the channel) is sound.

title: 1935 mill pond is half meadow: grass and vegetation never exclude the pond ellipse, and the dam reads as a boardwalk floating across grass
evidence: grep finds zero POND/pond references in src/grass.js and src/vegetation.js (they only exclude distToRiver/distToStreams zones), yet the pond's eastern half has terrain 184.5-186.1 (measured at (-100,-324)=186.07, (-115,-300)=185.58, (-112,-345)=184.59, dam centre (-122,-322)=185.04) — all below POND_LEVEL 186.3, i.e. under water in eras 3-4. Screenshots audit/e4-pond-S.png, e4-pond-E-high.png and crop-pond-dam.png show dense tall grass covering what should be open pond water, with the dam (src/eras.js:569-571, a single BoxGeometry 30x2.4x1.8 at fixed y=pondLevel-0.9) lying across the grass like a floating walkway, water visible under its east tip.
fix_hint: Skip grass/reed/pebble instances inside the pond ellipse when heightAt < POND_LEVEL+0.3 (the pond exists in the terrain carve permanently, so a static exclusion is fine); seat the dam on two end footings or drop its y to bed level and raise its height so it reads embedded.
why: Verified adversarially and could not refute. (1) Code: grass.js and vegetation.js contain zero pond references; their only water exclusions are distToRiver/riverLevelNear/LAKES rules (grass.js:311-315, 359-366; vegetation.js:379), while the pond basin carve (terrain.js:71-84) is a 56x38m ellipse extending ~40m from the river spline — outside the 16.5-21m grass exclusion band. (2) Node probe importing the real modules reproduced every number in the finding: POND=(-148,-324), POND_LEVEL=186.30, terrain 186.07/185.58/184.59/185.04 at the cited points (all below pond level), with the grass exclusion evaluating false at three of them (distToRiver 23-41m). (3) Runtime census in era 4: 1,825 instanced grass/flower instances inside the pond ellipse below 186.30, at bed heights 183.6-185.0. (4) Fresh screenshots (v-e4-pond-top.png, v-e4-dam-close.png, v-e3-pond-top.png in the audit scratchpad) show no pond in eras 3 or 4 — just the river channel — with meadow grass covering the pond's eastern half, the dam (eras.js:569-571, single BoxGeometry at fixed y=pondLevel-0.9) lying diagonally across dry grass like a boardwalk touching water only at its west tip, and the mill wheel dry on grass. Only trivial nuance: the dam's underside is below terrain at its centre, so it is embedded rather than literally floating, but it visually reads exactly as described.

title: Reeds stand in open water mid-channel on bends, and stranded on the dry pan elsewhere
evidence: src/vegetation.js:688-704 offsets reed clumps 11-15 m from RAW RIVER_PTS, but the water ribbon follows the Catmull-Rom spline which bulges off the polyline on bends (the same drift acknowledged for the wdRiver field in src/landuse.js:46-49). crop-B-nearshore.png (era 1, manor bend) shows a reed clump standing in open water ~1/3 of the way across the channel, poking through the surface; e1-A-east.png shows other reed stalks scattered on the dry sunken pan ~2 m below the adjacent water surface.
fix_hint: Place reeds along the fine sampled spline (like fineR in landuse.js) at offsets just outside the ribbon width (>=12.5 m), and reject positions where heightAt < level-0.3 (in the channel) as well as the existing > level+1.0 check.
why: Verified by exact numeric replication and independent screenshots. Code: src/vegetation.js:688-704 offsets reed clumps from RAW RIVER_PTS by side*(11-15) m in x only plus a ±11 m z-jitter, and the sole rejection test is ground-too-high (y > level+1.0) — nothing rejects positions inside the carved channel; the water ribbon (src/water.js:61-90,149) follows the Catmull-Rom spline at 11.8 m half-width, which bulges off the raw polyline on bends (acknowledged at src/landuse.js:46-49 and src/terrain.js:44-47). Replicating the placement loop bit-for-bit in node (same makeNoise(2211) rng sequence including the lakes loop, real heightAt) shows 343 of 908 river reeds stand inside the flat water surface (<11.3 m from the spline centerline) with blade tops above water level — one at 0.15 m from the centerline poking 0.54 m above the surface — plus 149 fully submerged, and 241 reeds sit on ground 1.2-2 m below water level at 11.3-18 m from the spline, i.e. on the carved pan at/beyond the noise-varying bank skirt (outer edge 12.9-17.3 m). My own era-1 close-ups (vr-mid-491.png, vr-mid-275.png, vr-reach-graze.png in the audit scratchpad) visually show seed-headed reed stalks rising out of open water mid-channel and stalks scattered on the sunken flat pan below the adjacent water surface, matching the original crop-B-nearshore.png and e1-A-east.png evidence. Minor nuance only: stranded reeds are never more than ~18 m from the spline, so the "dry pan" mode occurs on the carved apron just beyond the skirt rather than far out on the floodplain. The fix hint (sample the fine spline like landuse.js fineR, place outside ribbon width, and also reject heightAt < level-0.3) is sound.

title: No pebbles or channel-bed stones ever visible at the waterline — the stony-shallows rule produces nothing to see
evidence: src/vegetation.js:715-727 puts pebbles 8-15.5 m from raw river points at terrain height — that band is either covered by the opaque bank-skirt mesh (11.8 to ~13-17 m, water.js:159-284) or lies on the sunken pan away from the visual waterline; :730-740 bed stones (max ~0.7 m) sit on a bed carved 1.9 m below the surface (terrain.js:55), so none break the surface, defeating the ':728 largest shoulder out of the water' intent. Close-range screenshots e4-A-closeup.png / crop-A-edge.png (12 m range) and crop-B-nearshore.png show zero stones at any shoreline; every shore is bare sand band straight to water.
fix_hint: Anchor pebbles to the fine spline at the skirt outer edge (offset wOut+0-2 m) so they sit on the visible collar; for shallows stones, place a size-scaled subset at 9-11.5 m offsets with y forced to level-0.2 so tops pierce the surface near the rim.
why: Verified by code reading plus a quantitative in-page probe that decomposed all 4,155 placed stone instances against the real 'gauja' centerline and 'bankskirt' meshes: 2,538 stones are fully underwater (bed carved to y-1.9 per terrain.js:55, under 0.93-opacity water), 776 are hidden under the opaque bank skirt (water.js:159-284, spans 11.8m to 12.9-17.3m at y-0.5..y+0.07 while the shelf terrain below is at y-0.55), and 741 more sit below water level on the sunken pan beyond the skirt — ~97% of the feature is invisible. The 'largest shoulder out of the water' intent (vegetation.js:710-712,728) is effectively defeated: only 4 of ~1,200 bed stones break the surface anywhere on the 16.5 km river. Close-up screenshots confirm bare sand shorelines at the village reaches; the best skirt-piercing candidates near the village do not visibly render, and the best on-land stone is swallowed by meadow grass. Caveat: the finding's absolutes are slightly overstated — the probe found 25 skirt-piercers, 71 land stones above water level, and I screenshotted one clearly visible surface-breaking stone at (198,5021), ~5 km upstream of the village (crop-pv-surf-stone.png). This does not rescue the feature (roughly one visible stone per several hundred metres of bank, essentially none in the village reaches), so the defect and its low severity stand, and the proposed fix direction (anchor pebbles to the skirt outer edge; force shallow-stone tops above water level) matches the measured geometry.

title: 1935 background fields ~7x too small: 0.8 ha ellipses give 1.3 ha of crops per farm and 3.4% of tile arable
evidence: bgFieldsFor era 4 generates 334 fields for 204 farms (1.64/farm), rx 42-84 m, rz 28-54 m -> area 0.40-1.40 ha, mean 0.79 ha; total 2.65 km² = 3.4% of the 77.44 km² tile (era 3: 211 fields, 1.75 km², 2.3%). Hand-placed rawFieldsForEra adds only ~0.11 km² more. The researched 1929/1935 baseline is 171 farms >20 ha (typically 8-12 ha arable each) and ~25-30% of Vidzeme parish land under plough — the sim shows each viensēta with a single garden-plot-sized patch and a countryside that reads far too unfarmed for 1935.

why: All quantitative claims reproduce exactly against the current code. src/landuse.js:230-247 bgFieldsFor gives each kept farm 1-2 ellipses of rx 42-84 m, rz 28-54 m; running the actual code paths (real DWELLINGS_OSM, mulberry32, farmSiteKept) yields for era 4: 204 farms kept of 212 sites, 334 fields (1.64/farm), 0.40-1.40 ha per field (mean 0.79 ha), total 2.64 km² = 3.41% of the 77.44 km² tile (HM_SPAN=8800), i.e. ~1.29 ha of crops per farm; era 3: 211 fields, 1.74 km² (2.24%); rawFieldsForEra(4) adds only 0.109 km². An aerial era-4 screenshot (scratchpad/audit/era4-aerial.png) confirms the visual claim: the 1935 landscape is near-uniform meadow with tiny scattered field patches. Minor caveat: the reviewer's "171 farms >20 ha" figure is not sourced in the repo, but the finding's direction and rough magnitude (~5-7x underfarmed) hold regardless.

title: 2025 renders 32 km of gravel V-roads as dark asphalt identical to the P30
evidence: The requested P30 check itself passes: ROADS_OSM has 9 class-0 pieces, all ref P30/'P30;V299' (raw JSON: 9 highway=primary ways, all surface=asphalt), and roadRibbons builds ribbons for r.c<=1 with era-5 colour 0x393c40. But that single material (eras.js:136-139) also covers the 19 class-1 pieces (32.0 km — V299, V300, V309, V325), and raw osm-roads.json tags those surface=unpaved (x8) or gravel (x1), none asphalt. In era 5 every V-road therefore appears paved highway-black; only the dashed centreline distinguishes the P30.
fix_hint: In roadRibbons split the geometry/material by class in era 5: keep 0x393c40 for c===0, use a gravel grey-brown (e.g. ~0x7d766a) for c===1, matching the OSM surface tags already present in data/osm-roads.json.
why: All load-bearing claims verified against current code and a fresh era-5 screenshot. (1) src/eras.js:136-139 creates a single MeshLambertMaterial (era===5 ? 0x393c40 : 0x8d7c5f) and the loop at :142-144 folds every r.c<=1 road into one mesh with that material, so class-1 V-roads get the same asphalt-dark colour as the P30 in 2025; only the dashed centreline (:173, r.c===0) is class-restricted. (2) data/bake-roads.mjs:28 maps secondary and tertiary to class 1. (3) data/osm-roads.json: all 9 primary (P30) ways are surface=asphalt; class-1 ways are 9 unpaved + 1 gravel + 9 untagged, none asphalt (finding said "unpaved x8, gravel x1" — a minor undercount that does not weaken the defect). (4) Recomputed from ROADS_OSM: class 1 = 19 pieces, 32.0 km, exactly as claimed. (5) Screenshot audit/v299-junction-era5.png (era=5, cam over the P30/V299 junction) shows V299 and a second V-road rendered in the identical dark grey as the P30, distinguished only by the P30's white dashes. Severity med and the fix hint (per-class material split in era 5, gravel tone ~0x7d766a for c===1) are reasonable and consistent with the existing 0x8d7c5f pre-war colour.

title: Stale count in comment: '768' OSM buildings vs 496 actually baked
evidence: BUILDINGS_OSM has 496 entries. This is fully consistent with the raw data (507 building ways in data/osm-roads.json, 501 fully inside the clipped tile, ~5 dropped by the <18 m² rule in bake-roads.mjs:86), and 476 are drawn after eras.js skip zones — but the eras.js:206 comment claims 'every OSM building footprint (768 of them)', overstating by 55%. Likely a leftover from an earlier, larger bbox bake.
fix_hint: Update the comment to 496 (or make bake-roads.mjs write the count into the generated file so it can't drift).
why: eras.js:206 comment says "every OSM building footprint (768 of them)" but the era-5 code (eras.js:241-245) iterates BUILDINGS_OSM from src/geodata-osm.js, which has exactly 496 entries (verified by importing the module). title: Six farms exist in 1860 but vanish by 1935 — per-era independent RNG breaks site persistence
evidence: farmSiteKept seeds mulberry32(i*977 + era*131), so era-3 and era-4 kept sets are independent draws: 6 of the 130 sites kept in 1860 are absent in 1935. This contradicts the code's own premise ('viensēta names persist for centuries', geodata-osm.js header and eras.js:207-208) and the historical direction of change (farms were added by the 1920 reform, not removed).
fix_hint: Make the 1860 set a subset of the 1935 set, e.g. kept4 = rng(i)<0.96 and kept3 = kept4 && rng2(i)<(0.3/0.96), so no farm ever disappears between eras 3 and 4.
why: Executed the actual code: farmSiteKept (src/landuse.js:378-379) seeds mulberry32(i*977 + era*131), giving independent per-era draws (thresholds 0.6 for era 3, 0.96 for era 4). Running it over the 212 DWELLINGS_OSM sites yields 130 kept in 1860 and exactly 6 of those absent in 1935 (Stemiķi, Rūķīši, Ķīru ūdenstornis, Viesturi, Eglāji, Lejas Andrēni); all 6 pass bgSettlement's skip() filter so they really render in era 3 and vanish in era 4, along with their orchards (vegetation.js:445) and yard props (landuse.js:234). This contradicts the code's own comments (eras.js:207-210: 1935 = all viensēta sites, 1860 = ~60% of them, with the 1920 reform only adding farms; geodata-osm.js:5: names persist for centuries). One correction to the fix hint: the era-3 keep probability is 0.6, not 0.3, so the subset fix should be kept4 = rng(i)<0.96 and kept3 = kept4 && rng2(i)<0.6/0.96. Severity low is appropriate.

title: Skip-zone farms get fields and orchards but no farmhouse (13 orphan fields in 1935)
evidence: eras.js bgSettlement suppresses buildings via skip() (within 100 m of STEAD, 140 m of MANOR, 70 m of KROGS/BREZGA, 80 m of POND, 60 m of CAMP) — 9 dwellings including 'Neķina muiža', 'Brežģis', 'Nēķins 1/2' fall inside. But bgFieldsFor (landuse.js:228) and the orchard pass (vegetation.js:445) test only farmSiteKept, so 13 era-4 (8 era-3) crop ellipses plus apple clusters are generated for houseless sites, despite the landuse.js:371-372 comment that the shared rule ensures 'one farm never gets an orchard without a house'. Mitigated because hand-placed diorama buildings occupy those zones.
fix_hint: Export the skip() predicate (or the zone list) from landuse.js and apply it in bgFieldsFor and the vegetation orchard loop, or drop the 9 in-zone dwellings at bake time.
why: Reproduced exactly by executing the repo's own modules. eras.js:237-254 suppresses background dwellings via skip() zones (STEAD 100m, MANOR 140m, KROGS/BREZGA 70m, POND 80m, CAMP 60m) plus farmSiteKept, but bgFieldsFor (landuse.js:234) and the orchard pass (vegetation.js:445) test only farmSiteKept. Running the exact predicates over DWELLINGS_OSM yields precisely 9 in-zone kept sites in era 4 (Brežģis, Kaltu māja, Cimbulīši, Neķina muiža, Senkrasti, Rudiņi, Dadzis, Nēķins 2, Nēķins 1) generating 13 orphan field ellipses and 29 apple trees, and 6 sites / 8 fields in era 3 — matching the finding's counts and named dwellings. The landuse.js:375-377 comment stating the shared rule ensures 'one farm never gets an orchard without a house' confirms this violates intent. Mitigation is real (8 of 9 sites sit inside the manor/krogs zones occupied by hand-placed diorama buildings), so severity 'low' is fair. Only trivial inaccuracy: cited line numbers are off by a few lines versus current code.
